By Advs. Sri.A.J.Shaheer Sri.A.B.Jaleel Smt.Nazlin Jaleel Shri.Nijaz Jaleel Respondents: 1 The District Collector, Palakkad Civil Station, Palakkad, Pin - 678001. 2 The Thaluk Supply Officer, Chittoor Municipal Complexe, Fathima Junction, Chittoor, Palakkad, Pin - 678101. 2025:Ker:55320 W.P.(C) No.5570/2025 Thoufeeq vs The District Collector on 14 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59513572/ 1 :2: 3 The Station House Officer, Kozhinjampara Police Station, Kozhinjampara, Palakkad, Pin - 678555. By Adv.Sri. Dheeraj A.S., Government Pleader This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Been Finally Heard On 14.07.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: 2025:Ker:55320 W.P.(C) No.5570/2025 :3: N. Nagaresh, J. ````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````` W.P.(C) No.5570 of 2025 ````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````` Dated this the 14th day of July, 2025 Judgment
texts.facts: ~~~~~~~~~ The petitioner, who is Proprietor of a Rice Mill in Kozhinjampara of Palakkad District, seeks to direct the 1st respondent to release 6558 Kg. rice seized from the petitioner. 2. Respondents 2 and 3 conducted a search in the shop of the petitioner on 15.10.2024 and seized 6558 Kg. rice kept in 132 bags (1345 Kg. Raw Rice in 27 bags, 5179 Kg. Boiled Rice in 104 bags and 33 Kg. Kuthari in one bag). It was alleged that the rice seized is Ration rice 2025:KER:55320 obtained by the petitioner illegally. 3. The rice was forwarded to the Taluk Supply Officer (TSO) for verification and a crime was registered as 893/2024 alleging offences under Sections 3 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act. Now, the rice is stored in NFSA Warehouse at Kozhinjampara. The petitioner states that the rice was later inspected by a Committee under the Kerala Targeted Public Distribution System Order, 2021 and the Committee reported that only 33 Kg. Kuthari rice is ration rice. 4. The 1st respondent took steps to sell the rice under Section 6(A)(2) of the Essential Commodities Act. The petitioner was served with a notice under Section 6(B). The petitioner produced Bills/documents evidencing legal purchase of rice by the petitioner. The petitioner was then required to appear before the Sub Collector for a hearing. Thoufeeq vs The District Collector on 14 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59513572/ 2 2025:KER:55320 The petitioner appeared for hearing, produced all relevant documents and requested to release the rice seized. 5. The Collector passed Ext.P6 order dated 29.01.2025 stating that as the Kozhinjampara Police has registered a crime against the petitioner and the same is pending before the Court, the 1st respondent cannot allow the demand of the petitioner to return the rice without permission of the Court. The petitioner is before this Court aggrieved by the decision of the Collector. 6. The petitioner states that he has purchased the rice paying 2,21,660/- and the petitioner has the purchase bills, e-way bills and other documents to prove that the petitioner did not obtain the rice illegally for making unlawful gains. Even the Committee under the Kerala Targeted Public Distribution System Order, 2021 has reported that only 33 Kg. rice is ration rice. Therefore, the 2025:KER:55320 petitioner is entitled to get released the rice purchased by him legally, contends the petitioner. 7. The 2nd respondent filed a counter affidavit. The 2nd respondent stated that the petitioner submitted explanation to the notice directly to the District Supply Officer, on the basis of which a hearing was conducted by the ADM on 07.01.2025. At the time of personal hearing, the petitioner submitted that the 6558 Kg. rice that was seized by the Kozhinjampara Police and handed over to the Chittur Taluk Supply Officer is being sold with legitimate bills. The seized rice were available in the open market under the Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS) and hence the seized rice should be released as the rice has been purchased from various sources. The petitioner contended that even though all the bills were produced before the authorities at the time of the seizure. At the time of hearing, on verifying the 2025:KER:55320 records, it was found that authorized bills or authenticated documents were not produced at the time of the seizure, as per the mahazar of police and the Taluk Supply Officer. Hence, the argument of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable. 8. The 2nd respondent further submitted that since FIR No.893/2024 was registered at Kozhinjampara Police Station and the court proceedings are underway, it is not possible to consider the demand of the petitioner to release the rice. The District Collector has ordered on 29.01.2025 (Ext.P6) that action can be taken subject to the court decision and the order has been served on the petitioner. The petitioner has not challenged Ext.P6 order. On 15.10.2024, rice weighing 6558 Kg. was seized from the shop of the petitioner. The seizure was on an allegation that the rice is ration rice illegally procured by the petitioner. A case has been registered against the petitioner under the Essential Commodities Act. The rice is at present in the NFSA Warehouse at Kozhinjampara. The petitioner would contend that he possesses all the documents to show that the rice is legally procured by him. Even the Committee under Kerala Targetted Public Distribution System has reported that only 33 Kg. rice out of the 6558 Kg. rice, is Thoufeeq vs The District Collector on 14 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59513572/ 3 ration rice. 11. If the petitioner can establish the afore facts, then the petitioner is legally entitled to get the rice released. However, a crime is now registered and a case is pending before the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Chittoor. As the case is pending before the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, the petitioner has to approach the Magistrate's Court for custody / getting release rice.
